message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"55757596c92eed9e9e81a72b026f29439d839d5117a07250bb119ed275beaec5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:70","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","units":[{"unit_id":"sec05-u01","module_id":"sec05-m01","objective_ids":["sec05-u01"],"title":{"text":"Tire pressure and tread","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Tires are the one part of road safety fully within your control, and neglected tires cause preventable crashes.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02"]},{"text":"Two quick checks, pressure and tread, catch most tire problems before they become dangerous.","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F07","sec05-R02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ana checks her tires on a cool morning and her gauge reads higher than the doorframe sticker.","fact_ids":["sec05-F04","sec05-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When the gauge shows more than the doorframe number, you release air until the two readings agree.","fact_ids":["sec05-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Ana lets out air until the gauge matches the sticker, then does the penny test on each tire.","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that seeing all of Lincoln's head in the penny test means the tread is fine.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]},"correction":{"text":"If all of Lincoln's head is visible, the tread is too worn and the tires should be replaced.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Cold tires, door sticker, match the numbers; whole head showing means new tires.","fact_ids":["sec05-F06","sec05-F04","sec05-F08"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"What should you do if all of Lincoln's head shows during the penny test?","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"Stop driving on those tires and have them replaced.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"A fully visible head means the tread is too worn to be safe.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Tires you can trust","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Maintenance is in your control","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F07"]},{"text":"Two quick checks","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"You cannot control other drivers or the condition of the road, but you can control how well your own vehicle and tires are maintained. Crashes caused by neglected tires are preventable, and tires that are under-inflated, over-inflated or low on tread all create safety problems. In this unit you will learn two simple checks that every driver can do at home: a monthly pressure check with a gauge and a quick tread check with a penny. Together they take only a few minutes and protect you every time you drive. A tire problem caught at home is far easier to fix than one found on the highway.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Checking tire pressure","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Check every month with a gauge","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06"]},{"text":"Target is on the doorframe sticker","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06"]},{"text":"Measured in pounds per square inch","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Check your tire pressure every month using a tire pressure gauge, and buy one if you do not already own one. The correct pressure for your vehicle is the number printed on a sticker on the inside doorframe, so note it before you measure. Tire pressure is measured in pounds per square inch. To take a reading, remove the cap from the valve stem and press the gauge evenly onto it. Measure while the tires are still cold, before a long drive warms them up, so the reading is accurate. These checks take only a few minutes, and the payoff is a safer trip every time.","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Adjusting to the right number","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F02","sec05-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Gauge above sticker: let air out","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F02","sec05-F04"]},{"text":"Gauge below sticker: add air","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F02","sec05-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Once you have a reading, compare it with the doorframe number. When the gauge shows more pressure than the doorframe number, you release air. When it shows less, you add air. Keep adjusting and rechecking until the two readings agree. Both under-inflated and over-inflated tires create safety problems, so the goal is not simply more air but the exact number on the sticker. Make this part of your monthly routine, and recheck any tire that seems to lose air faster than the others between checks. Make the monthly check a habit, such as on the first weekend of each month.","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F02","sec05-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The penny tread test","fact_ids":["sec05-R02","sec05-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hold the penny by Lincoln's body","fact_ids":["sec05-R02","sec05-F07"]},{"text":"Push it head first into a groove","fact_ids":["sec05-R02","sec05-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Tread depth is a separate check from pressure. The gauge measures pressure, while the penny measures tread, so they are two different inspections and you need both. For the penny tread test, hold a penny by Lincoln's body and push it, Lincoln's head first, into the groove that looks deepest. Then look at how much of his head you can see. Repeat the check on each tire, because tread can wear unevenly. The result tells you whether the tires still have enough tread to grip the road safely. Write down the doorframe number so you have it handy for every check.","fact_ids":["sec05-R02","sec05-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Reading the penny correctly","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Whole head visible: too worn","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Replace the tires","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers think that seeing all of Lincoln's head means the penny went in cleanly and the tread is fine. It means the opposite. If all of Lincoln's head is visible in the groove, the tread is too worn, so do not drive on those tires and have them replaced. Deep tread would hide part of his head. Remember that the penny result is about tread, not pressure: a perfectly inflated tire can still be worn out, and only the penny check will reveal it. Both pressure and tread matter, so never skip one because the other looks fine.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Quick tire check","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-F07","sec05-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Penny test result","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-F07","sec05-F03"]},{"text":"All of Lincoln's head shows","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-F07","sec05-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you do the penny test and can see all of Lincoln's head in the deepest groove. What should you do? The answer is to stop driving on those tires and have them replaced. A fully visible head means the tread is too worn. If the tread were deep enough, it would cover part of his head. Combine this check with your monthly pressure check on cold tires, adjusting to the doorframe number, and your tires will rarely surprise you on the road. A cheap gauge and a single penny are all the tools you need for these checks. Good tires help you stop, steer and stay in control when it matters most.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-F07","sec05-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Tire care recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R01","sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Monthly gauge check on cold tires","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R01","sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Match the doorframe number","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R01","sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Whole head showing means replace","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R01","sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, tire care is the part of road safety you fully control, and neglected tires cause preventable crashes. Check pressure every month with a gauge on cold tires, compare it with the number on the inside doorframe, measured in pounds per square inch, and let air out or add air until the readings agree. Then check tread with a penny held by Lincoln's body and pushed head first into the deepest groove. If all of his head shows, the tread is too worn and the tires must be replaced. Checking every tire, not just one, gives you a complete restraint","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before you start the engine, set your seat and mirrors. Doing it first lets you see clearly, fully control the pedals and steering wheel, and leaves room for an air bag to deploy. In this unit you will learn how to sit, how your foot should reach the pedals, where the steering wheel should sit, how much distance to keep from it, and how to set the head restraint. Each adjustment takes seconds, and together they make the vehicle's safety systems work the way they were designed to protect you. Every adjustment here supports the safety systems built into your vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Posture and pedal reach","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Back against the seat, feet down","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},{"text":"Foot pivots, heel on the floor","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Sit upright with your back against the seat and your feet on the floor, because slouching can make the vehicle's restraint system less effective. In a correct seat position, your foot pivots smoothly from the brake to the accelerator while your heel stays on the floor. If you have to lift your whole leg to move between pedals, the seat is too far back. If your knees are cramped against the dash, it is too far forward. Find the position where the pivot feels natural and your back stays against the seat. Take care of these settings before every drive in a shared vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Wheel height and distance","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wheel top no higher than shoulders","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F10"]},{"text":"At least ten inches from your chest","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F10"]},{"text":"Do not recline the seat","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"The top of the steering wheel should be no higher than the tops of your shoulders. Leave a gap of at least ten inches from your chest to the steering wheel, never move the seat so far forward that steering becomes hard, and do not recline the seat. That distance leaves room for an air bag to deploy, which is one reason the manual asks you to adjust before driving. If you are short, raise the seat rather than sliding closer than ten inches; if you are tall, move back until the gap is right. The steering wheel and the head restraint both have position rules, but they work differently. The steering wheel limit is about height, with its top no higher than your shoulders. The head restraint limit is about contact: it should touch the back of your head and not sit below your ears. Head restraints are meant to prevent whiplash, so one resting at the base of your neck does little good. Check both, because getting one right does not mean the other is right too. Then confirm the rest of your setup: upright posture, a foot that pivots between the pedals with the heel down, a wheel no higher than your shoulders, and a head restraint touching the back of your head. Once set, these positions should feel natural rather than forced.","fact_ids":["sec05-F13","sec05-F09","sec05-F11","sec05-F12","sec05-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Seat setup recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-F11","sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F14","sec05-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Upright, heel down","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-F11","sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F14","sec05-R05"]},{"text":"Wheel below shoulders, ten inches back","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-F11","sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F14","sec05-R05"]},{"text":"Head restraint on the head","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-F11","sec05-F12","sec05-F13","sec05-F14","sec05-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, adjust your seat and mirrors before you start driving so you can see clearly, control the pedals and wheel, and leave room for the air bag. Sit upright with your back against the seat, and let your foot pivot between the pedals with your heel on the floor. Keep the top of the wheel no higher than your shoulders and at least ten inches from your chest, without reclining. Finally, set the head restraint so it touches the back of your head, not below your ears, to help prevent whiplash. outside mirrors barely show the car.","fact_ids":["sec05-R03","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Where should your head be when you set the left outside mirror with the enhanced method?","fact_ids":["sec05-F17"]},"answer":{"text":"Rest your head against the closed left window and adjust until the vehicle's rear edge barely shows.","fact_ids":["sec05-F17"]},"rationale":{"text":"The left mirror method uses the left window as your head position.","fact_ids":["sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Seeing behind and beside you","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Rearview mirror is primary","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-F16"]},{"text":"Outside mirrors cut blind spots","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Your mirrors are your view of everything behind and beside you, so setting them well matters as much as setting your seat. The rearview mirror, the interior mirror mounted on the windshield, is your primary mirror for seeing what is behind you. The outside mirrors cover the sides and help shrink blind spots, the areas where your view is blocked. In this unit you will learn how to set the rearview mirror, how to use the enhanced method for each outside mirror, and what you gain by doing it. Good mirror habits support every lane change and every stop.","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The rearview mirror","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Frame the whole rear window","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03"]},{"text":"Set a day-night mirror for the time","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Set the rearview mirror so it frames the whole rear window. If your vehicle has a day-night mirror, switch it to suit the time of day you are driving. Because the rearview mirror is your primary view behind you, check it often in normal driving, especially before slowing, stopping or changing lanes. A mirror tilted toward the back seat or the headliner leaves you guessing about traffic behind you. Before every drive, once seated, confirm it still shows the full rear window. Recheck your mirrors whenever another driver has used the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Enhanced outside mirror settings","fact_ids":["sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Left: head against left window","fact_ids":["sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},{"text":"Right: lean to center console","fact_ids":["sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},{"text":"Vehicle edge should barely show","fact_ids":["sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Outside mirrors are set to shrink blind spots and give the widest possible view to the sides and rear. For the enhanced left mirror setting, rest your head against the closed window on your left and adjust the mirror until the rear edge of your vehicle barely shows. The right mirror uses a different method: lean right until your head is under the rearview mirror or over the center console, then adjust until the right edge of your vehicle is just visible. Then return to your normal seated position. Mirrors work best when combined with quick head checks.","fact_ids":["sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Hiding your own car on purpose","fact_ids":["sec05-F18","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your car's sides disappear","fact_ids":["sec05-F18","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},{"text":"You gain extra side view","fact_ids":["sec05-F18","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. When you sit normally after using the enhanced settings, you will not see your own vehicle's sides when you glance at the outside mirrors. Many drivers think that means the mirrors are set wrong and tilt them back in. Do not. The enhanced settings hide your own sides on purpose, and in exchange they add twelve to sixteen degrees of extra viewing area on each side. Seeing your own doors wastes mirror space; seeing the lanes beside you is what helps you change lanes safely. A few seconds of setup can prevent a missed vehicle beside you.","fact_ids":["sec05-F18","sec05-F17","sec05-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Quick mirror check","fact_ids":["sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Enhanced left mirror","fact_ids":["sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},{"text":"How do you set it?","fact_ids":["sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: how do you set the left outside mirror using the enhanced method? The answer is to rest your head against the closed window on your left and adjust the mirror until the rear edge of your vehicle barely shows. For the right mirror, lean right until your head is under the rearview mirror or over the center console and adjust until the right edge is just visible. When you sit back normally, your own sides disappear and you gain extra view on each side. The right settings make every glance more useful. Clear mirrors also help you spot faster traffic coming up behind.","fact_ids":["sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Mirror setup recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03","sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Rearview frames the rear window","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03","sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},{"text":"Enhanced left and right methods","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03","sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]},{"text":"Twelve to sixteen degrees gained","fact_ids":["sec05-F15","sec05-R03","sec05-F16","sec05-F17","sec05-R04","sec05-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, the rearview mirror is your primary view behind you; set it to frame the whole rear window, and switch a day-night mirror to suit the time of day.
